definitions.explanation: A facial expression created with text characters, used in digital communication to convey emotions. Japanese kaomoji are typically read horizontally and use a wider variety of characters than Western emoticons.

examples.japanese: {顔文字|かおもじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
⟦メール→メール：04435_meeru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{顔文字|かおもじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{柔|やわ}らかい→柔らかい：01096_yawarakai⟧⟦{印象|いんしょう}→印象：01846_inshou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Adding emoticons to emails gives a softer impression.

examples.japanese: ⟦ビジネス→ビジネス：11162_bijinesu⟧⟦メール→メール：04435_meeru⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{顔文字|かおもじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}わない→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦ほうがいい→ほうがいい：10078_hougaii⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It is said that you shouldn't use emoticons in business emails.

notes:
Literally 'face character' (⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧ face + ⟦{文字|もじ}→文字：03632_moji⟧ character). Refers to emoticons made from text characters, such as (^_^) or (T_T). Japanese kaomoji are distinct from Western emoticons in that they are read face-on (not tilted sideways) and often use a much wider set of Unicode characters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {顔文字|かおもじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧: to use emoticons
- {顔文字|かおもじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧: to insert an emoticon
- {顔文字|かおもじ}⟦{一覧|いちらん}→一覧：17694_ichiran⟧: list of emoticons

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{絵文字|えもじ}→絵文字：13859_emoji⟧: emoji — pictographic characters (now a global term); distinct from text-based kaomoji
- ⟦スタンプ→スタンプ：11577_sutanpu⟧: LINE stickers — image-based expressions used on the LINE messaging app

CULTURAL NOTE:
Kaomoji became hugely popular in Japan during the early internet era and remain widely used in casual text messages and social media. Common examples include (^_^) for happiness, (T_T) for crying, and (>_<) for frustration.
